title: Harbourside FC — Financial Report
subtitle: FY 2025/26 · management accounts · narrated by Pit Wall

scenes.heading: The year in one line
scenes.say: Welcome to Harbourside's financial report for the twenty twenty-five, twenty twenty-six season. The club earned one hundred nineteen million euros, turned a four point one million euro operating profit, and kept squad spending at sixty-eight percent of revenue, just inside the league's seventy percent limit.

scenes.heading: 1 · Revenue — where the money comes from
scenes.say: Revenue comes from three places. Broadcast rights are the biggest, at sixty-two million. Commercial and sponsorship deals add thirty-one point four million. And matchday and season tickets bring in twenty-five point eight. Together, one hundred nineteen point two million euros.

scenes.heading: 2 · Player trading — unique to football
scenes.note: A bought player is a capital asset. Selling him above his written-down value books a profit — Harbourside's sales added €12.6M this year.
scenes.say: Here's the part unique to football. A player the club buys is a capital asset on the books. When Harbourside sells one for more than his written-down value, the difference is a profit. Player sales added twelve point six million this year.

scenes.heading: 3 · Costs — what the club spends
scenes.note: Wages + amortisation + agent fees are what the league's 70% squad-cost cap is measured against.
scenes.say: On the cost side, wages are the big one, at forty-four point four million. Each bought player is written down over his contract — twenty-one million in amortisation this year. Add sixty-two million of other running costs, and total spend is one hundred twenty-seven point seven million.

scenes.heading: 4 · The result — does it add up?
scenes.say: Put it together. Income of one hundred thirty-one point eight million, against costs of one hundred twenty-seven point seven, leaves an operating profit of four point one million. And the club holds eight point nine million in cash. Harbourside is living within its means.

scenes.heading: 5 · Every number ties back
scenes.say: And every figure here is built from the ledger. A hundred and ninety-eight journal entries, a trial balance that balances to the cent, and an audit trail that can explain any number with a single query. That's the whole point of Pit Wall: autonomous, but accountable.
